title: Remark
body_md: We use $\xrightarrow{\makebox[1em][c]{$\scriptstylep$}}$ and $\xrightarrow{\makebox[1em][c]{$\scriptstyled$}}$ for convergence in probability and in distribution respectively. We will throughout use standard Mann-Wald notation to describe orders of magnitude of quantities. Given two sequences of positive constants $(a_n), (b_n)$, we write $a_n = o(b_n)$ when $\lim_{n \to \infty} (a_n/b_n) = 0$, and $a_n = O(b_n)$ when $\limsup_{n \to \infty} (a_n/b_n) = K < \infty$. For a sequence of random variables $\{X_n\}$ and a sequence of positive constants $\{a_n\}$, we write $X_n = o_p(a_n)$ if $X_n / a_n \xrightarrow{\makebox[1em][c]{$\scriptstylep$}} 0$ as $n \to \infty$; and $X_n = O_p(a_n)$ when $X_n / a_n$ is bounded in probability as $n \to \infty$ i.e. $\lim_{C \to \infty}\limsup_{n\to\infty}\mathbb{P}(|X_n|\ge Ca_n)=0$. In particular, for a constant $c$, $X_n = c + o_p(1)$ means that $X_n \xrightarrow{\makebox[1em][c]{$\scriptstylep$}} c$.

title: Proof
body_md: By definition $d_{\mathrm{geo}}(z,z') = r \arccos(\langle\hat{n},\hat{n}'\rangle)$. Proposition~\ref{prop:sphere_backprojection}(ii) gives $d_{\mathrm{geo}}(z,z')= r\arccos\,\bigl(\sqrt{1 - \|v\|^2/r^2}\bigr) = r\arcsin\,\bigl(\|v\|/r\bigr)$, using $\arccos(\sqrt{1-u^2}) = \arcsin(u)$ for $u \in [0,1]$. This proves \eqref{eq:geodesic_exact}. The function $u\longmapsto (\arcsin^2u-u^2) /u^4$ is nonnegative and extends continuously to $[0,1]$, with a value of $1/3$ at $u=0$. Its boundedness gives the claimed bound \eqref{eq:geodesic_expand}.

label: lem:factorisation
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Asymptotic factorisation

title: Proof
body_md:
Write $\|v\|^2 = M_d(1 + \eta_d)$ where $\eta_d := \|v\|^2/M_d - 1$. Then
\[
  \mathbb{E}_\pi[\|v\|^2 \cdot a]
  = M_d \mathbb{E}_\pi[a] + M_d \mathbb{E}_\pi[\eta_d \cdot a].
\]
Since $0 \le a \le 1$, Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
  |\mathbb{E}_\pi[\eta_d a]|
  \le \mathbb{E}_\pi[\eta_d^2]^{1/2} \mathbb{E}_\pi[a^2]^{1/2}
  \le \mathbb{E}_\pi[\eta_d^2]^{1/2}
  = O(d^{-1/2}),
\]
using \eqref{eq:eta_L2}. Hence $M_d \mathbb{E}_\pi[\eta_d a] = o(M_d)$.

title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:scalar_markovianity}
The sequences $t_k:=t(z_k)$ and $(t_k,X_k)$ are time-homogeneous Markov chains. Their transition kernels preserve the corresponding images of $\pi_d$; in particular, the scalar kernel preserves \eqref{eq:t_density}. The same statements hold for the intrinsic proposal \eqref{eq:intrinsic_proposal}.
head: environment
name: Markovianity

title: Proof
body_md: The scalar proposal and acceptance probability are measurable functions of $(t(z),\xi_1,W)$ and the law of $(\xi_1,W)$ does not depend on $z$. At $t=\pm1$, the choice of the tangent basis is irrelevant. For the pair, orthogonal transformations fixing both $b$ and $e_{\perp}$ act transitively on each set of states with a given $(t,X)$, and the proposal, projection and acceptance are equivariant under these transformations. Thus each projected transition law depends only on the corresponding projected state. Preservation of the image laws follows from invariance of $\pi_d$, its image under $z \mapsto t(z)$ preserves the density \eqref{eq:t_density}. The same argument applies after the constant rescaling of drift and noise in \eqref{eq:intrinsic_proposal}.

title: Remark
body_md: The acceptance probability in Theorem~\ref{thm:fixed_step} is averaged over the stationary distribution. This average has a positive limit, although the conditional acceptance probability at the point $z=b+r\hat b$ tends to zero as $d\to\infty$ at fixed $\beta$. Consequently, at fixed $\beta$, there is no dimension-independent bound on the total-variation mixing time that holds uniformly over initial states. This distinction between stationary and nonstationary acceptance seems analogous to the transient behaviour of MALA for which certain initial conditions require smaller proposal scales than those in stationarity \cite{christensen-roberts-rosenthal:2005,jourdain-lelievre-miasojedow:2014}.

label: lem:good_event
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: The good event $\Omega_d$

title: Proof
body_md:
The tail bound:
$\mathbb P(\Omega_d^{\complement})
 \le \mathbb P(W>\tfrac32 d) + \mathbb P(\xi_1^2>\tfrac14 d)
 \le e^{-cd}$
by standard Chernoff bounds for $\chi^2_{d-2}$ and $\chi^2_1$. By $(a+b)^2\le 2a^2+2b^2$, $|c_\beta|\le\beta$ and $\|P_z(b)\|^2\le\delta^2 d$,
\begin{equation*}
  \|v\|^2 \le 2c_\beta^2\|P_z(b)\|^2 + 2\beta^2\xi_1^2 + \beta^2 W
  \le 2\beta^2\delta^2 d + \beta^2\bigl(W+2\xi_1^2\bigr)
  \le 2\beta^2 d\,(1+\delta^2)
\end{equation*}
on $\Omega_d$; the choice of $\beta_0$ gives $\le\kappa^2 d/2 = r^2/2$. The final claim holds since $\|v\|^2/r^2\le\tfrac12$ on $\Omega_d$.

label: lem:acceptance_moments_diffusion
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:acceptance_moments_diffusion}
Let $\xi_1\sim\mathcal{N}(0,1)$, assume $C_*\ne0$, and let $R_0$ be as in \eqref{eq:g0_R0_diffusion}. Then
\begin{align}
    \mathbb{E}[\mathcal A(R_0)]&= 2\Phi(-\sigma_\ell/2),
\label{eq:A_moment_diffusion}\\
    \mathbb{E}\!\left[\left(\xi_1-\frac{C_*\tau\ell^3}{2}\right) \mathcal A(R_0) \right]&=0,
\label{eq:A_first_moment_disappears}\\
    \mathbb{E}\!\left[\left(\xi_1-\frac{C_*\tau\ell^3}{2}\right)^2 \mathcal A(R_0) \right] &=K(\sigma_\ell),
\label{eq:K_moment_diffusion}\\
\mathbb{E}\!\left[\left(\xi_1-\frac{C_*\tau\ell^3}{2}\right)e^{R_0}\mathds1_{\{R_0<0\}}\right]
&= \frac{C_*\tau\ell^3}{2}\Phi(-\sigma_\ell/2) -\operatorname{sgn}(C_*)\phi(\sigma_\ell/2)\,,
\label{eq:derivative_moment_diffusion}
\end{align}
where $K$ is defined in \eqref{eq:K_diffusion}. In particular, $K(\sigma_\ell)>0$.
